reason: The hypothesis synthesizes two separate findings from the literature: (1) temperature accelerates the formation of a more protective, Fe3+-rich passive film on Q235 steel in a simulated concrete pore solution (P21, P23, P30), and (2) Q235 steel corrosion in saline/chloride environments is controlled by mass transfer (P2, P8). It links these through a new mechanistic proposal—that the temperature-enhanced film directly suppresses mass-transfer-driven corrosion in a harsh chloride environment—which no single passage states. This integration of passivation kinetics with a specific corrosion control mechanism goes beyond the individual sources.
copied_elements: temperature-dependent passivation of Q235 steel (P21, P23, P30)
higher temperature leads to faster passivation and more Fe3+ compounds (P21, P23, P30)
Q235 corrosion is mass-transfer controlled (P2, P8)
